cards.explanation: The answer is men to spy out the land. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Send out for yourself men to spy out the land of Canaan…” (Numbers 13:2). These men are going to look around and bring back what they see. Scouts, not soldiers, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Moses, “From each of their fathers’ tribes send one man who is a leader among them.” (Numbers 13:2). So every tribe gets a seat on this trip. Nobody gets left standing at the curb, friends.

The answer is how strong they are and how many. Moses, Israel's leader, tells the spies to see “…whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.” (Numbers 13:18). He wants to know the size of the crowd and the strength of the crowd. Remember that question, bakers, because the answers come back later.

The answer is True. Moses, Israel's leader, tells the spies to check, “Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?” (Numbers 13:19). So they're not only sizing up the people, they're looking at where the people live. I'd have sent one guy to count the walls and another to look for a back door.

The answer is fruit. Moses, Israel's leader, tells the spies, “Be courageous and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (Numbers 13:20). He asks for fruit, and he asks them to be courageous in the same breath. The text also adds that it was the season for the first ripe grapes.
The answer is Anak. The text calls Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai “…the descendants of Anak…” (Numbers 13:22). They live in Hebron. Keep the name Anak in your pocket, friends, because it comes up again.

The answer is on a pole between two men. The text says the spies cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, “…which they carried on a pole between two men.” (Numbers 13:23). One pole, two men, one cluster. That cluster was not a snack-size situation, friends.
The answer is False. Besides the grapes, “They also took some pomegranates and figs.” (Numbers 13:23). The cluster gets the big headline, but it had company. Quite a haul from one valley, bakers.

The answer is flowing with milk and honey. The spies tell Moses, Israel's leader, “…it is flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27). They start with good news, and they have the fruit right there to show it. Hold onto this part, friends, because the report is about to turn.

The answer is strong. The spies say, “…the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are large and fortified.” (Numbers 13:28). Remember Moses asked if the people were strong or weak (Numbers 13:18). Now they're giving him their answer, bakers.

The answer is Caleb. The text says, “Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said…” (Numbers 13:30). Caleb is the spy from the tribe of Judah (Numbers 13:6). Quieting a crowd is a real talent, friends. I can't even quiet my oven timer.

The answer is conquer. Caleb, the spy from the tribe of Judah, says, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!” (Numbers 13:30). He doesn't say maybe, and he doesn't say we'll see. He says certainly, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, “So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out…” (Numbers 13:32). These are the men who answered Caleb with, “We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!” (Numbers 13:31). Caleb said go, and they said no, bakers.

The answer is False. Their bad report says, “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.” (Numbers 13:32). They never call the land too dry to grow anything. Earlier they said it's “…flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27), and they showed the congregation the fruit (Numbers 13:26).

The answer is like grasshoppers. The men who went up with Caleb say, “We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight…” (Numbers 13:33). That's how small they felt next to the people they saw. I think a grasshopper standing next to a mountain would understand that feeling, friends.
